newsitem.title: UK: JP Morgan silent on taking stake in Polish bank.
newsitem.headline: JP Morgan silent on taking stake in Polish bank.

text.p: U.S. investment bank J.P. Morgan and Co Inc declined to comment on Tuesday on a report it was discussing taking a stake in Poland's Bank Handlowy.

A J.P. Morgan spokeswoman declined to comment on the report in Tuesday's Wall Street Journal which said the bank was in talks with the Polish government to "take a leading stake in a privatised Bank Handlowy".
Poland is offering a total of 95 percent or 61,750,000 shares of Handlowy in a privatisation scheme which begins later this month.
The Wall Street Journal said the Polish government would increase the bank's capital by 43 percent and begin an initial public offering of 31.5 percent of Handlowy's expanded share capital on Monday.

The paper said J.P. Morgan was in talks to lead a group of core investors which would hold 30 percent of the bank's post-privatisation shares, would take an active role in overseeing the bank and would hold the shares for at least three years.
It said talks were focusing largely on price.
